analyzed_vuln.description: The recursion bound check is off by one relative to `CtxJson::commaNeeded[100]`. `writeJsonObjStart` permits `ctx->depth == 99`, increments it to 100, and then writes `ctx->commaNeeded[100]`, although valid indices are 0..99. The same pattern exists for array starts, but this PoV reaches the object-start path through `DiagnosticInfo_encodeJson`. Additionally, the DiagnosticInfo encoder's comment claims `encodeJsonInternal` checks recursion, but that dispatcher performs no such check, so a decoded recursive DiagnosticInfo chain reaches the unsafe boundary. The observed crash occurs during `UA_calcSizeJson`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Attacker-controlled JSON is decoded by the fuzz harness as a reversible Variant whose Body is a DiagnosticInfo (Type 25) containing a sufficiently deep chain of present, non-null `InnerDiagnosticInfo` objects. `DiagnosticInfoInner_decodeJson` allocates and recursively decodes that chain without applying the context recursion limit. The harness then calls `UA_calcSizeJson`; the outer Variant object plus nested DiagnosticInfo object starts raise `ctx->depth` to 99, and the next nonempty DiagnosticInfo calls `writeJsonObjStart`, which increments to 100 and indexes past `commaNeeded`. The supplied permissively tokenized JSON constructs such a chain within the 1000-token limit.

I am considering changing both start checks to reserve the post-increment slot and adding an explicit early recursion check to DiagnosticInfo_encodeJson so a failed start does not continue recursively. Please assess depth semantics and whether decode also needs adjustment for a root-cause, functionality-preserving patch.
